questions.prompt: Describe the to-do manager's four layers and how data flows through them in one run. Name which class owns user interaction, the domain model, business logic and persistence, then trace a run from start-up loading through a menu action to the final save, and state the pattern the codebase map wants you to notice.

keyPoints.text: App.java is the entry point and the CLI interaction layer.
keyPoints.quote: `src/todo/App.java` is the entry point and CLI interaction layer.

keyPoints.text: Task is the domain model and TaskManager is the in-memory business logic layer.
keyPoints.quote: `src/todo/service/TaskManager.java` is the in-memory business logic layer.

keyPoints.text: TaskRepository is the persistence layer.
keyPoints.quote: `src/todo/repository/TaskRepository.java` is the persistence layer.

keyPoints.text: App.run() loads tasks from TaskRepository and passes the loaded Task objects into TaskManager.
keyPoints.quote: Loaded `Task` objects are passed into `TaskManager`.

keyPoints.text: The menu loop reads a choice and App calls the matching TaskManager method, which updates the list or a Task.
keyPoints.quote: `App` calls the matching `TaskManager` method.

keyPoints.text: When the program exits, App asks TaskRepository to save the latest list to disk.
keyPoints.quote: When the program exits, `App` asks `TaskRepository` to save the latest list to disk.

keyPoints.text: Pattern: input and output stay in App, rules in TaskManager, state in Task objects and the manager's list, persistence in TaskRepository.
keyPoints.quote: rules stay in `TaskManager`

questions.prompt: What are the app's runtime boundaries, and what does it deliberately not have? Then explain the three complexity hotspots the codebase map names, what makes each risky, and what a new Task field drags along with it.

keyPoints.text: Terminal I/O: reading menu choices and printing output.
keyPoints.quote: Terminal I/O: reading menu choices and printing output

keyPoints.text: In-memory domain state: the task list while the app runs; file persistence: reading and writing tasks.txt.
keyPoints.quote: File persistence: reading from and writing to `tasks.txt`

keyPoints.text: Time: timestamps are created at runtime with LocalDateTime.now().
keyPoints.quote: timestamps are created at runtime using `LocalDateTime.now()`

keyPoints.text: There are no network calls, databases, background jobs or auth systems.
keyPoints.quote: There are no network calls, databases, background jobs, or auth systems in this project.

keyPoints.text: TaskRepository is the most format-sensitive file: a small parsing or serialization change can break saved data.
keyPoints.quote: A small change in parsing or serialization can break saved data.

keyPoints.text: App coordinates several responsibilities and can grow too large if features are added casually.
keyPoints.quote: It is easy for this file to become too large if new features are added casually.

keyPoints.text: TaskManager owns id generation, so creation-rule changes must keep ids stable.
keyPoints.quote: If creation rules change, id stability needs to stay intact.

keyPoints.text: A new Task field likely needs updates in both the repository and the display logic.
keyPoints.quote: If you add new fields to `Task`, you will likely need to update both the repository and display logic.

questions.prompt: What design intent does the codebase map infer, and which task invariants does it ask you to protect? Cover the three likely goals of the split, the one-decision-per-class idea, the rule about where business rules must not go, the title, completedAt and deletion invariants, and where the title rule is actually enforced given what Task's constructor does.

keyPoints.text: Likely intent: keep main thin and keep file I/O away from user interaction logic.
keyPoints.quote: keep file I/O away from user interaction logic

keyPoints.text: Make the task rules easy to change without rewriting the CLI.
keyPoints.quote: make the task rules easy to change without rewriting the CLI

keyPoints.text: Each class is meant to own one kind of decision.
keyPoints.quote: Each class is meant to own one kind of decision.

keyPoints.text: Do not put business rules into App just because the menu loop can reach it.
keyPoints.quote: Do not put business rules directly into `App` just because it is easy to reach from the menu loop.

keyPoints.text: A valid task's title should not be blank.
keyPoints.quote: `title` should not be blank for valid tasks.

keyPoints.text: completedAt should stay null for incomplete tasks, so completed and completedAt must stay consistent.
keyPoints.quote: `completedAt` should stay `null` for incomplete tasks.

keyPoints.text: Deleting a task should remove it permanently from the next saved file.
keyPoints.quote: Deleting a task should remove it permanently from the next saved file.

keyPoints.text: Task's constructor stores the title without checking it, so the blank-title rule lives at the entry points (the CLI prompt and the repository's load check), not in the model.
